note.zh-TW: 和銷貨債權增加(-) 是同一科目的兩個方向，同一期的報表只會用到其中一列；這是網站照課程模板填寫的做法。
note.en: This and the increase line are two directions of the same account, and a single period’s statement uses only one of them; this is how the site follows the course template.

definition.zh-TW:
間接法裡的調整列：本期應收帳款比期初少了多少。

應收帳款減少代表以前賒銷的貨款收回來了，這筆現金不在本期的收入裡，所以要加回稅前淨利。
definition.en:
An adjustment line in the indirect method: how much trade receivables have fallen since the start of the period.

A fall in receivables means earlier credit sales have been collected; that cash is not part of this period’s revenue, so it is added back to profit before tax.

example.zh-TW: 位置：現金流量表營業活動的營運資金變動區。課程模板替應收帳款設了兩列：淨增加填在銷貨債權增加(-)，淨減少填在這一列；同一期的報表只會用到其中一列。台灣現行報表每個科目只有一行淨變動。
example.en: Where it sits: the working capital section of operating activities in the statement of cash flows. The course template gives receivables two lines: a net increase goes on increase in trade receivables (-), a net decrease on this line; a single period’s statement uses only one of them. Current Taiwanese statements show a single net movement per account.

misconception.zh-TW: 把收回貨款當成本期的收入再算一次。收入早在賒銷那期就認列了，收款只是把應收帳款換成現金；這一列的作用就是把這筆「有現金、沒收入」的差額補回來。
misconception.en: Counting the cash collected as revenue again. Revenue was recognised when the credit sale was made; collection merely swaps a receivable for cash. This line exists to add back that cash-but-no-revenue difference.
